name: StrongLifts
tagline: A barbell workout tracker built around the 5x5 linear progression program, with plate math, timers and progress charts.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. Free tier plus a paid Pro subscription.

verdictSummary: The core of this app is a spreadsheet with a rest timer. Three lifts per workout, alternating A/B days, add 2.5kg when you hit all reps, deload 10 percent after three failures: that is the entire algorithm and it fits in about forty lines of code. Plate math, warmup sets and a countdown between sets are all trivially derivable from the working weight. What you are actually paying for is a polished native app that never loses your log and does not need thought at 6am in a loud gym, which a local web build approximates but does not match.
coreLoopDIY: Logs each set of a fixed A/B 5x5 barbell routine, auto-progresses or deloads the next session's weight, shows the plates to load per side, and runs a rest timer.
requirements: A phone browser that supports IndexedDB and can install a PWA
A way to export or back up local data yourself
whatYouLose: A real native app with reliable background timers, notifications and an Apple Watch companion
Cloud backup and multi-device sync, so a wiped browser is a wiped training log
Apple Health and Google Fit write-back
Guided form videos, exercise explanations and the program coaching content
Support for the many program variants, accessory lifts and custom routines the paid tier ships with
moatNotes: The moat is being the default answer when someone googles 5x5, plus fifteen years of not corrupting anyone's training history.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because gym software gets used in a bad environment: sweaty hands, no signal, forty-five seconds between sets, and zero patience for a UI that requires reading. StrongLifts has had a very long time to sand that down, and it syncs so your log survives a new phone. A self-built PWA covers the math perfectly well and honestly might be nicer if you only run one program, but you own the backups, and you will find out the hard way what that means.
notes: The rarer case on this list: the domain logic really is that small, and the paid product is mostly delivery.
prompt:
Build a local-first strength training tracker as an installable PWA. No backend, no accounts, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite, React, TypeScript, Tailwind, Dexie (IndexedDB) for storage, vite-plugin-pwa for the manifest and service worker. No server, no auth, no external API calls.

Program model (hardcode this, single user):
- Workout A: Squat 5x5, Bench Press 5x5, Barbell Row 5x5.
- Workout B: Squat 5x5, Overhead Press 5x5, Deadlift 1x5.
- Sessions alternate A, B, A, B in order.
- Progression: if all prescribed reps are completed, next session for that lift adds 2.5 kg (5 kg for deadlift). Otherwise the weight repeats.
- Deload: after 3 consecutive failed sessions on a lift, cut the weight by 10 percent, rounded down to the nearest 2.5 kg, and reset the failure counter.

UI, three screens:
1. Today: which workout is up, each lift with 5 tappable set buttons that cycle 5 reps down to 0, a plate-loading readout per side computed from a configurable bar weight and available plates, and a rest timer that starts automatically on set tap (90s under 3 failed reps, 180s otherwise) with a visible countdown and a Web Audio beep at zero. Big touch targets, readable at arm's length, dark by default.
2. History: reverse chronological list of finished sessions with weights and reps, tappable to edit.
3. Progress: one line chart per lift of working weight over time. Use a tiny chart lib or hand-rolled SVG, your call, pick one and commit.

Settings: kg or lb, bar weight, plate inventory, starting weights per lift, JSON export and JSON import for backup.

Requirements: works fully offline after first load, state survives reload and app close, no data leaves the device. Include a README with setup, how progression and deload work, and a blunt warning that browser storage can be cleared so export regularly. Seed the DB on first run with empty-bar starting weights.
